rationale: The student touched the same bear twice while counting to 8, confusing one-to-one correspondence. A number-line demonstration showing single sequential hops starting from 0 models counting each item exactly once.

script.focus: each hop matching one count without repeating

intent: Demonstrate add on the number-line with values [0,6]. Tutor points at: each hop matching one count without repeating

content.title: Counting on, one hop at a time

frames.caption: Start at 0. We are standing here; we have not hopped yet.
Hop 1 moves one forward and lands on 1. The first number we count is where we land, not where we started.

judgement.reasoning: The student struggles with one-to-one correspondence when counting discrete physical objects (bears), double-counting or skipping objects. The chosen detour uses a continuous number line showing 0 + 6 = 6 via hopping, which is an abstract addition concept far beyond the kindergarten student's immediate need to track and tag physical objects accurately.
judgement.verdict: A teacher would not use an addition number-line demonstration to remediate a kindergarten student's lack of one-to-one correspondence when counting discrete objects.
